## Summary of the change

Between SCOPe 2.04 and current SCOPe (2.08, frozen 2021-07-28, released 2021-09-22, latest periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16), the ColG collagen-binding domain and the Cry3A C-terminal domain went from having **no asserted evolutionary relationship at all** to being **sibling families inside one superfamily**. The change happened at SCOPe 2.05, not gradually across releases.

**SCOPe 2.04.** PDB 1nqd (Clostridium histolyticum ColG collagenase collagen-binding domain 3b, 1.65 A, with calcium) contributed two whole-chain domains, d1nqda_ (sunid 86025) and d1nqdb_ (sunid 86026), both classified b.23.2.1: class b (all-beta proteins), fold b.23 CUB-like (sunid 49853), superfamily b.23.2 Collagen-binding domain (sunid 89260), protein Class 1 collagenase (sunid 89262), species Clostridium histolyticum TaxId 1498 (sunid 89263). PDB 1dlc (Cry3A / CryIIIA insecticidal delta-endotoxin, 2.5 A) was split into three domains, and its C-terminal domain d1dlca1 (sunid 23719, A:500-644) was b.18.1.3: fold b.18 Galactose-binding domain-like (sunid 49784), superfamily b.18.1 Galactose-binding domain-like (sunid 49785), family b.18.1.3 delta-Endotoxin, C-terminal domain (sunid 49796), species Bacillus thuringiensis tenebrionis CRYIIIA (BT13) TaxId 1444 (sunid 49798). The two domains therefore shared only class b. SCOPe treats class as a descriptive bin, so in 2.04 the database made no homology claim whatsoever between them; they sat in different folds, which is the explicit statement that not even a shared topology was recognised.

**Current SCOPe 2.08.** d1nqda_ keeps sunid 86025 but is now b.18.1.36: same fold b.18 and same superfamily b.18.1 Galactose-binding domain-like, in a newly created family b.18.1.36 Collagen-binding domain (sunid 267607), protein Class 1 collagenase (sunid 267633), species Clostridium histolyticum TaxId 1498 (sunid 267693). d1dlca1 is unchanged at b.18.1.3 (and its sibling domains d1dlca2 b.77.2.1 and d1dlca3 f.1.3.1 are also unchanged). So the pair is now **same class, same fold, same superfamily, different family**.

**Mechanics of the move.** The old collagen-binding superfamily was not renamed, it was dissolved. b.23.2 resolves in 2.04 but returns 404 in 2.05 and in 2.08; the CUB-like fold b.23 now contains only b.23.1 Spermadhesin CUB domain, b.23.3 Acetamidase/Formamidase-like and b.23.4 Complement system CUB domain. Reciprocally, superfamily b.18.1 grew from 33 families in 2.04 (ending at b.18.1.33) to 35 in 2.08, the additions visible here being b.18.1.36 Collagen-binding domain and b.18.1.37 Clostridium perfringens enterotoxin (CPE), C-terminal domain. b.18.1.36 did not exist in 2.04 (404). Querying d1nqda_ release by release shows b.18.1.36 already in 2.05, 2.06 and 2.07, so the reclassification was a 2.05 curation event that has been stable for four releases.

The move came with a domain-boundary cleanup on chain B. In 2.04 chain B was one whole-chain domain d1nqdb_; in 2.08 it is d1nqdb1 (B:893-1008, b.18.1.36) plus d1nqdb2 (B:891-892, sunid 281794, l.1.1.1 artifact). Chain A remains a single whole-chain domain. The 2.08 family now also holds d1nqja_, d1nqjb_, d2o8oa_, d2o8ob2, d4hpka_, d4hpkb_ and the tandem-CBD domains d5ikua1 and d5ikua2 from 5iku, the last two flagged as automated matches to d1nqda_.

## What the new placement does and does not claim

Superfamily is SCOPe's weakest level that still asserts common ancestry. Placing ColG CBD in b.18.1 says curators judge a probable common evolutionary origin with the delta-endotoxin C-terminal domain, inferred from structure and from shared ligand-binding architecture, in the absence of detectable sequence similarity. It deliberately stops short of family, which would require convincing sequence-level evidence or clear functional equivalence. The two remain in separate families (b.18.1.36 vs b.18.1.3), so SCOPe is explicitly not claiming orthology, a shared ligand, or transferable function.

## Structural evidence

From the live API, FATCAT structural comparison supports the superfamily grouping, and the significant cross-family hit runs from the collagenase side. Chain 1nqdA is not an ASTRAL cluster representative; its representative is 1nqjA at 99.16% identity over 119 alignment columns, and the API warns that representative matches must not be attributed directly to the requested chain. With that caveat, 1nqjA structure hits include:

| Hit | SCCS and family | p-value | RMSD (A) | Seq identity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| d5ikua1 | b.18.1.36 Class 1 collagenase | 4.2e-14 | 1.72 | 28.7% |
| d2quoa_ | b.18.1.37 CPE C-terminal domain | 1.4e-06 | 2.49 | 10.3% |
| d1wmfa1 | b.18.1.20 proprotein convertase P-domain | 2.0e-06 | 1.84 | 12.9% |
| d1w99a3 | b.18.1.3 delta-Endotoxin C-terminal domain (Cry4Ba) | 3.95e-03 | 2.52 | 2.5% |

Nineteen of the 100 hits fall in b.18.1, the strongest enrichment in the list, which is itself evidence that the CBD belongs to this superfamily rather than to CUB-like. From the toxin side, 1dlcA hits within b.18.1 are d2qkga3 (b.18.1.0 automated matches, p 2.98e-05, RMSD 1.42 A), d1w99a3 (b.18.1.3, p 2.0e-04, RMSD 1.43 A), d1ux7a_ (b.18.1.28 CBM28 endo-1,4-beta-xylanase D, p 7.46e-03, RMSD 2.37 A, 12.5% identity) and d1w9wa_ (b.18.1.10 CBM6-like, p 7.6e-03, RMSD 1.58 A, 9.5% identity). Cry3A domain III therefore itself cross-matches carbohydrate-binding modules of the superfamily, independent of the collagenase.

The underlying architecture is the same in both: a compact beta-sandwich of roughly 110 to 150 residues, two mostly antiparallel sheets in a jelly-roll-like, lectin-like topology, with the ligand-binding surface built from the loops and sheet face at one end of the sandwich. ColG CBD3b (1nqd, about residues 893-1008) carries two bound Ca2+ ions near the N-terminal region that rigidify the sandwich, and its collagen-binding surface is a linear array of exposed residues on one beta-sheet face. Cry3A domain III (1dlc A:500-644) is the same sandwich decorated differently, with no equivalent calcium site.

**Critical limit on the structural evidence.** There is no direct, statistically significant pairwise FATCAT hit between the ColG CBD and the Cry3A domain of 1dlc in either hit list. The structural bridge is indirect: ColG CBD matches Cry4Ba domain III (d1w99a3), which is in the same family b.18.1.3 as Cry3A domain III, and Cry3A domain III matches CBM6 and CBM28 modules of the same superfamily. The ColG-to-Cry4Ba alignment is marginal (p 3.95e-03, 2.5% identity, 2.52 A over about 95 to 113 aligned residues on each side), which is near noise level for identity. The superfamily assignment rests on a chain of weak pairwise matches plus curator judgment, not on one convincing ColG-to-Cry3A superposition.

## Functional evidence

The shared, and genuinely informative, functional signature is **modular accessory targeting**, not a shared chemistry. Both domains are non-catalytic recognition modules appended to an effector module in a secreted bacterial protein. ColG CBD anchors the collagenase onto insoluble collagen fibrils and is required for efficient degradation of fibrillar, as opposed to soluble, collagen; the peptidase activity itself lives in a separate, unrelated catalytic domain of ColG, not in the CBD. Cry3A domain III mediates binding to insect midgut brush-border receptors, including aminopeptidase N and cadherin-like proteins, and carbohydrate or glycan recognition by domain III is documented for Cry toxins (N-acetylgalactosamine binding in Cry1Ac domain III); the pore-forming activity lives in the unrelated helical domain I (d1dlca3, f.1.3.1).

The superfamily context reinforces this reading. b.18.1 is dominated by surface-recognition beta-sandwich modules: the galactose-binding domain, discoidin/FA58C, CBM4/9, CBM6, CBM11, CBM15, CBM17, CBM22, CBM27, CBM28, CBM29, CBM30, CBM36, fucose-binding lectin, PA-IL galactose-binding lectin, the ephrin receptor ligand-binding domain, XRCC1 N-terminal, APC10-like and the proprotein convertase P-domain. Both ColG CBD and Cry domain III fit that pattern as substrate- or receptor-targeting appendages. The strongest functional parallel in the current data is the neighbouring family b.18.1.37, the Clostridium perfringens enterotoxin C-terminal domain, a bacterial toxin host-surface recognition module that the API's FATCAT run matches to ColG CBD at p 1.4e-06 and RMSD 2.49 A. Bacterial secreted toxins and secreted degradative enzymes have evidently recruited this same beta-sandwich scaffold repeatedly as a targeting module, which is the functional argument for one ancestral ligand-binding sandwich diversifying into collagen binding, glycan binding and receptor binding.

## Limits on homology and function transfer

- **Do not transfer function between the families.** Cry3A domain III does not bind collagen, and the ColG CBD confers neither midgut receptor binding nor insecticidal pore formation. What is inherited is a scaffold and a generic ligand-binding surface, not a ligand. Specifically, there is no basis for treating either domain as conferring toxicity or protease activity on the other.
- **Do not read catalysis into the fold.** Neither domain is catalytic. Collagenolysis belongs to ColG's peptidase domain and lysis to Cry3A domain I.
- **Family-specific features are not superfamily signatures.** The two Ca2+ sites of ColG CBD are a family elaboration, absent from the delta-endotoxin family; calcium dependence must not be projected onto b.18.1.
- **Templates.** At about 2.5 A RMSD with near-zero sequence identity, Cry domain III is unusable as a comparative-modeling template for the CBD beyond the sandwich core. The loops that carry binding specificity are precisely the parts that do not align, so any model of the collagen-binding surface built from the toxin would be unreliable. Use the within-family structures (1nqj, 2o8o, 4hpk, 5iku) instead.
- **Representative selection.** Report FATCAT numbers for 1nqjA, not 1nqdA. Here the 99.16% identity makes transfer defensible, but the provenance should be stated. Likewise, d5ikua1 and d5ikua2 are automated matches to d1nqda_, not manually curated placements, and the b.18.1.0 automated-matches family (which supplied the 1dlcA hit d2qkga3) carries no manual homology assertion.
- **Release scope.** SCOPe 2.08 was frozen 2021-07-28, so Cry toxin or bacterial collagenase structures released after that date are absent or appear only through automated matches. The relationship as described is a 2.05-to-2.08 curation state, not a live reflection of the PDB.

## External evidence that would strengthen or settle the case

The current support is structure-led and marginal at the sequence level, so independent lines are needed: profile-profile and HMM-HMM comparison (HHpred/HHsearch, HMMER against Pfam, comparing Pfam Collagen_bind PF09262 with the Cry domain III family Endotoxin_C PF03944); agreement from independent classifications (CATH and ECOD assignments for the galactose-binding/concanavalin-like beta-sandwich region, and InterPro/Gene3D); DALI or TM-align Z-scores to complement the FATCAT p-values; ligand-complex crystallography showing whether the binding surfaces occupy homologous positions on the sandwich; mutagenesis of the ColG CBD collagen-binding face and the Cry domain III receptor-binding loops to test whether function maps to equivalent structural elements; and phylogenetic analysis of CBM-bearing clostridial and bacillus secreted enzymes and toxins to test a single ancestral module rather than convergent recruitment. Without at least profile-level sequence support or independent classification agreement, the superfamily grouping should be quoted as a curator-inferred probable common origin, which is exactly the strength SCOPe 2.08 asserts.
